items.quote: Washington, D.C., officially the District of Columbia and commonly known as Washington, is the federal capital city of the United States
The south bank of the Potomac River forms the district's border with Virginia
In 1791, L'Enfant designed the baroque-styled plan for the development of Washington, D.C.
items.note: Andrew Ellicott revised and published the plan in 1792 after L'Enfant was dismissed, so a pedant may say Ellicott; "original 1791 plan" already rules him out. Accept "Peter Charles L'Enfant".

items.quote: commemorating the March 27, 1912, gift of Japanese cherry trees from Mayor Yukio Ozaki of Tokyo City to the city of Washington, D.C.
items.note: Strictly the gift was from the city of Tokyo (Mayor Ozaki), not the national government; "Tokyo" should also be accepted. Answer is right.

items.quote: James Smithson (c. 1765 – 27 June 1829) was a British chemist and mineralogist
items.note: Answer is right, but the same article says he was "Born in Paris, France" and given the French name Jacques-Louis Macie, so a room can fairly argue "French", and "English" is also correct. Suggested rewording: "The Smithsonian Institution was founded with money left by a British scientist who never visited America. What was his surname?" Answer: Smithson (James Smithson). Also note the question half gives the answer away (Smithsonian / Smithson) either way, which is fine as an easy one.
